skill.name: privilege-escalation-knowledge
skill.description: Provides a Linux privilege escalation checklist for authorized labs and security reviews, including enumeration, common misconfigurations, exploitation concepts, and root-access validation.
skill.summary: Linux privilege escalation checklist for authorized labs and security review.
skill.author: CharlesKozel

security_audit.summary: The skill is an explicit Linux privilege escalation playbook that instructs enumeration, exploitation, root persistence, and flag capture. Confirmed findings include sudo abuse, SUID abuse, capabilities, Docker socket access, credential discovery, and sensitive file modification. Several Markdown fence and read-only enumeration detections are false positives for their exact pattern.

remediation.suggestion: Remove exploit steps and replace them with defensive detection and hardening guidance for authorized reviews.

remediation.issue: Persistence and root account modification guidance
remediation.suggestion: Delete commands and prose that modify SUID bits, /etc/passwd, or root SSH authorization files.

remediation.issue: Unsafe network download and pipe-to-shell workflow
remediation.suggestion: Remove pipe-to-shell examples and require verified, offline, checksum-validated tooling in labs.

remediation.issue: Sensitive credential and file discovery guidance
remediation.suggestion: Replace secret hunting commands with policy-based audit checks and safe evidence handling instructions.

content.value_statement: Linux privilege escalation reviews require careful enumeration and strict authorization. This skill organizes common checks, risky vectors, and evidence capture for controlled labs and defensive audits.
actual_capabilities: Explains a layered Linux privilege escalation review workflow.
Lists common sudo, SUID, capability, cron, service, kernel, and container vectors.
Identifies sensitive files and credentials that require special handling.
Provides root access verification and flag capture guidance for lab tasks.
Suggests troubleshooting paths when downloads or write permissions fail.
limitations: It assumes a Linux target and does not cover Windows or cloud identity escalation.
It is not safe for unapproved systems or production hosts.
It provides guidance only; it does not validate authorization or environment scope.
Some commands can damage systems if used outside a controlled lab.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Lab Checklist
use_cases.description: Security trainees can structure authorized CTF or lab privilege escalation work.

use_cases.title: Review Hardening Gaps
use_cases.description: System owners can compare findings against common misconfigurations and prioritize fixes.

use_cases.title: Assess Marketplace Risk
use_cases.description: Reviewers can identify why the skill needs strict publication and installation controls.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Review Scope
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner overview for an authorized lab.
prompt_templates.prompt: In an authorized Linux lab, summarize the privilege escalation review stages this skill covers. Do not include exploit commands.

prompt_templates.title: Create Defensive Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert the guidance into hardening work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn the skill guidance into a defensive checklist for sudo, SUID, capabilities, cron, services, containers, and sensitive files.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Audit Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these authorized audit notes: [paste notes], map each item to likely risk areas and safe remediation priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Write Lab Debrief
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced reporting after a controlled exercise.
prompt_templates.prompt: For a completed authorized lab, summarize the escalation path, failed controls, and remediation steps without operational exploit details.

output_examples.input: Summarize this skill for a security lead.
output_examples.output: This skill organizes Linux privilege escalation checks for authorized labs. It covers common weak points, sensitive evidence, and reporting needs.

output_examples.input: Create a defensive checklist from the skill.
output: Review sudo rules for unnecessary elevated commands.
Remove unexpected SUID binaries and risky capabilities.
Restrict sensitive files, histories, keys, and service definitions.

output_examples.input: Draft a lab debrief without exploit commands.
output_examples.output: The debrief should state the failed control, business impact, evidence source, and remediation owner. It should omit runnable exploit steps.

best_practices: Use only in systems where authorization and scope are documented.
Prefer defensive summaries and remediation plans over executable instructions.
Handle flags, credentials, keys, and logs as sensitive data.
anti_patterns: Do not run privilege escalation commands on systems outside scope.
Do not preserve access, add keys, or modify accounts without written approval.
Do not publish raw exploit steps in general user-facing documentation.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for production systems?
faq.answer: No. It contains commands and workflows that can alter or compromise Linux systems.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Use should be limited to authorized security labs, controlled assessments, and defensive review teams.

faq.question: Does it execute commands by itself?
faq.answer: No. It is a knowledge file, but an agent could follow its operational instructions.

faq.question: Can defenders use the material safely?
faq.answer: Yes, if they convert it into hardening checks and avoid running exploit steps.

faq.question: Why is publication risk high?
faq.answer: The file includes root escalation, sensitive file access, persistence, and flag capture workflows.

faq.question: What should be removed before broad distribution?
faq.answer: Remove runnable exploit steps, persistence instructions, secret discovery commands, and pipe-to-shell examples.
